title: Potential molecular mechanisms underlying the ameliorative effect of Cola nitida (Vent.) Schott & Endl. on insulin resistance in rat skeletal muscles.
authors: Erukainure, Ochuko L; Oyebode, Olajumoke A; Chuturgoon, Anil A; Ghazi, Terisha; Muhammad, Aliyu; Aljoundi, Aimen; Elamin, Ghazi; Chukwuma, Chika I; Islam, Md Shahidul
one_liner_zh: 该文研究可乐果浸液对糖尿病大鼠骨骼肌胰岛素信号通路基因表达的影响，并辅以分子对接和分子动力学模拟评估植物成分与靶蛋白的结合，虽涉及蛋白-DNA互作较少，但分子模拟方法可借鉴于TF-DNA体系。
abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Cola nitida (Vent.) Schott & Endl. are among the common medicinal plants employed in traditional medicine for treating diabetes and its complications. AIM OF THE STUDY: The present study investigated the effect of Cola nitida infusion on the expression of key genes involved in insulin signaling vis-a-vis Insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS-1), tumor protein P53 gene, glucose transporter type 4 (GLUT4), phosphoinositide 3-kinases (PI3K) and B-cell lymphoma-2 (BCL2) in skeletal muscles of type 2 diabetic (T2D) rats. METHODS: Type 2 diabetic rats were administered C. nitida infusion at low and high doses (150 and 300 mg/kg bodyweight, respectively), while a high dose of the infusion was also administered to a normal toxicological group. Metformin served as the standard antidiabetic drug. The rats were sacrificed at the end of the experimental period. Their psoas muscles were harvested and assayed for the expressions of IRS1, p53, GLUT4, PI3K and BCL2. The studied genes were further subjected to enrichment analysis using the ShinyGO 0.76 online software. RESULTS: Induction of T2D upregulated the expressions of IRS-1, p53, PI3K and BCL2 in psoas muscles, while concomitantly downregulating GLUT4 expression. These expressions were significantly reversed in type 2 diabetic rats treated with C. nitida infusion, and the results were statistically significant compared to metformin. Gene enrichment analysis revealed that the genes were linked to intrinsic pathways and biological processes involved in insulin resistance. The infusion further improved muscle glucose uptake, ex vivo. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics stimulation of C. nitida infusion phytoconstituents, caffeine and theobromine with IRS-1, p53, GLUT4, PI3K and BCL2 revealed a strong binding affinity as evident by the RMSD and RMSF values. CONCLUSION: These results indicate the potentials of C. nitida infusion to improve glucose homeostasis in skeletal muscles of type 2 diabetic rats.
abstract_zh: 民族药理学相关性：可乐果（Cola nitida (Vent.) Schott & Endl.）是传统医学中用于治疗糖尿病及其并发症的常见药用植物之一。研究目的：本研究探讨了可乐果浸剂对2型糖尿病（T2D）大鼠骨骼肌中参与胰岛素信号传导的关键基因表达的影响，包括胰岛素受体底物1（IRS-1）、肿瘤蛋白P53基因、葡萄糖转运蛋白4型（GLUT4）、磷脂酰肌醇3-激酶（PI3K）和B细胞淋巴瘤-2（BCL2）。方法：对2型糖尿病大鼠给予低剂量和高剂量（分别为150和300 mg/kg体重）的可乐果浸剂，同时将高剂量浸剂也给予一个正常毒理学组。二甲双胍作为标准抗糖尿病药物。实验期结束时处死大鼠，采集其腰肌并检测IRS1、p53、GLUT4、PI3K和BCL2的表达。所研究的基因进一步使用ShinyGO 0.76在线软件进行富集分析。结果：诱导T2D上调了腰肌中IRS-1、p53、PI3K和BCL2的表达，同时下调了GLUT4表达。在经可乐果浸剂治疗的2型糖尿病大鼠中，这些表达显著逆转，且与二甲双胍相比结果具有统计学显著性。基因富集分析显示，这些基因与参与胰岛素抵抗的内在通路和生物学过程相关。浸剂还改善了离体肌肉的葡萄糖摄取。可乐果浸剂植物成分咖啡因和可可碱与IRS-1、p53、GLUT4、PI3K和BCL2的分子对接和分子动力学模拟显示，RMSD和RMSF值表明其具有强结合亲和力。结论：这些结果表明可乐果浸剂具有改善2型糖尿病大鼠骨骼肌葡萄糖稳态的潜力。
